title: Tidy Landmark Survival Analysis
text: Provides tidy framework landmark survival analysis, facilitating construction landmark-specific risk sets, incorporation longitudinal covariates, estimation associations time--event outcomes. Supports covariate estimation using last observation carried forward (LOCF) linear mixed-effects models (LME), alongside Cox proportional hazards Fine-Gray competing risks regression. Offers consistent reproducible workflow conducting analyses across multiple landmark times.

title: Tidy Landmark Survival Analysis
text: fit_landmark() fits separate survival model landmark. Supply one-sided survival formula; outcome built internally risk set’s follow-time status. model death (cause = 2). transplant competing event, default Cox model estimates cause-specific hazard ratios. tidy() returns one row per landmark term, number events behind estimate origin term (baseline, LOCF LME). Landmarks estimated keep row status, don’t silently drop results. Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models use model = "finegray", summary() shortcut exponentiated tidy() output. native survival::coxph() fit landmark kept fit$models.
code: # Fit a cause-specific Cox model at every landmark fit <- lm_cov |>   fit_landmark(     formula = ~ age + log_bili + albumin + edema,     cause = 2   )  fit #> <landmark_fit> Cause-specific Cox model for cause 2 at 5 landmark(s) #> Formula: ~age + log_bili + albumin + edema #> Horizon: 180 (relative to each landmark) #>  landmark n_eligible n_model n_event n_competing fit_status #>       365        290     290       4           1         ok #>       730        278     278      14           4         ok #>      1095        245     245       8           0         ok #>      1460        225     225       5           2         ok #>      1825        202     202       5           3         ok #>  #> Standard errors treat LME-derived covariates (log_bili, albumin) as known. #> Use tidy() for coefficients and summary() for hazard ratios. # Hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals fit |>   tidy(exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>   dplyr::select(.landmark, term, estimate,                  conf.low, conf.high, origin, n_event) |>    head() #> ℹ Standard errors treat LME-derived covariates as known, so they understate #>   uncertainty. #>   Bootstrap intervals that account for this are planned for a future release. #> This message is displayed once per session. #> # A tibble: 6 × 7 #>   .landmark term     estimate conf.low conf.high origin   n_event #>       <dbl> <chr>       <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>      <int> #> 1       365 age         1.07  0.971         1.18 baseline       4 #> 2       365 log_bili    1.63  0.557         4.79 lme            4 #> 3       365 albumin     0.128 0.000182     90.0  lme            4 #> 4       365 edema      12.4   0.731       209.   locf           4 #> 5       730 age         1.06  0.999         1.11 baseline      14 #> 6       730 log_bili    3.67  1.98          6.80 lme           14 # Fine-Gray model for death, with transplant as a competing event lm_cov |>   fit_landmark(~ age + log_bili + albumin + edema,                 model = "finegray", cause = 2) |>   summary() |>   dplyr::select(.landmark, term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, .fit_status) |>    head() #> Warning: 1 of 5 landmark models did not fit cleanly. #> • Landmark 1095 (warning): no competing events: estimates equal the Cox model #> ℹ Unestimable and failed landmarks have no estimates. See `$model_info` for #>   details. #> # A tibble: 6 × 6 #>   .landmark term     estimate conf.low conf.high .fit_status #>       <dbl> <chr>       <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>       #> 1       365 age         1.07  0.974         1.17 ok          #> 2       365 log_bili    1.63  0.910         2.93 ok          #> 3       365 albumin     0.128 0.000370     44.3  ok          #> 4       365 edema      12.4   0.514       297.   ok          #> 5       730 age         1.06  0.995         1.12 ok          #> 6       730 log_bili    3.67  2.08          6.48 ok

text: add_landmark_covariates() adds one column per selected longitudinal variable landmark_tbl. every subject-landmark row, value derived subject's measurements taken landmark, information landmark leaks covariates. variable derived one two ways: locf: last observation carried forward, optionally limited lookback window. lme: subject-specific value landmark predicted linear mixed-effects model fitted separately every variable landmark. Rows never added removed, .time/.status untouched. Subjects usable measurement keep row missing value.

code: add_landmark_covariates(   landmark_data,   longitudinal_data,   id,   time,   locf = NULL,   lme = NULL,   include_at_landmark = TRUE,   lookback = NULL,   lme_args = list(),   names = NULL,   progress = getOption("tidylandmark.progress", interactive()) )

title: Attach pre-landmark covariates to a landmark dataset — add_landmark_covariates
text: landmark_data landmark_tbl, returned landmark_data() (previous call add_landmark_covariates()). longitudinal_data data frame one row per measurement occasion (multiple rows per subject). Rows whose id appear landmark_data ignored, number reported message. id <tidy-select> subject identifier column longitudinal_data. must non-missing type id used landmark_data(); types never coerced implicitly. time <tidy-select> Numeric, finite, non-missing measurement time. must time scale origin time given landmark_data(); checked automatically. Measurements time zero (e.g. screening visits) allowed. locf, lme <tidy-select> Columns longitudinal_data derive last observation carried forward linear mixed-effects model, e.g. locf = c(treatment, stage) lme = c(bili, albumin). Either may NULL (default), . Rename inside selection name derived column, e.g. lme = c(bili_lme = bili). lme variables must continuous numeric. include_at_landmark TRUE (default), measurement taken exactly landmark (\(t = s\)) may used. FALSE, measurements strictly landmark (\(t < s\)) used. Applies methods. lookback locf . NULL (default) carries values forward without limit. single non-negative number uses measurements within window: \(s - t \le\) lookback. Older values give NA. lme_args lme . named list model options: random_slope: FALSE (default) fits random intercept; TRUE adds random slope time. adjust: NULL (default) one-sided formula fixed-effect adjustment terms, e.g. ~ age + sex. Variables come landmark_data, baseline values (covariates added earlier call). Use .t time since landmark, e.g. ~ sex * .t sex-specific slopes. REML: passed lme4::lmer(). Default TRUE. control: lme4::lmerControl() object. Default lme4::lmerControl(). min_subjects: fewest subjects measurements needed fit model (default 5). random_slope = TRUE, many subjects must least two measurements. names NULL (default) template derived column names, "{.col}" replaced source variable "{.method}" "locf" "lme", e.g. "{.col}_{.method}". Columns renamed selection keep new name. derived name already exists landmark_data error; existing columns never overwritten. progress Show progress bar fitting mixed models? Defaults tidylandmark.progress option, interactive() unset.

title: Attach pre-landmark covariates to a landmark dataset — add_landmark_covariates
text: landmark_data one new column per selected variable (locf columns first, lme), appended existing columns. class configuration kept, configuration records derived column made: method, source variable, options, LOCF audit trail, LME fitted models diagnostics. printed header lists derived columns method.

title: Attach pre-landmark covariates to a landmark dataset — add_landmark_covariates
text: landmark \(s\), subject \(\) variable \(v\), value last non-missing measurement \(v\) time \(t \le s\) (\(t < s\) include_at_landmark = FALSE), provided within lookback. variable handled separately, visit one variable missing still contributes others. Selection depends id time, never row order. column type works, type (including factor levels) preserved. time since carried-forward measurement stored metadata auditing. subject two different non-missing values locf variable time, function errors lists affected subjects times rather choosing one arbitrarily. Exact duplicates collapsed.

title: Attach pre-landmark covariates to a landmark dataset — add_landmark_covariates
text: every lme variable \(v\) landmark \(s\), independent Gaussian model fitted lme4::lmer() non-missing measurements, taken \(s\), subjects risk set \(s\): $$Y_{ij} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 (t_{ij} - s) + \gamma^\top x_i + b_{0i} [+ b_{1i}(t_{ij} - s)] + \epsilon_{ij}$$ \(x_i\) optional adjust terms. Time centred landmark rescaled internally numerical stability, change predictions. derived value conditional prediction \(t = s\) including subject's random effects (predict(fit, re.form = NULL)), .e. \(\hat\beta_0 + \hat\gamma^\top x_i + \hat b_{0i}\). subject single measurement kept; prediction shrunk towards population trajectory. subject measurement landmark, missing adjust values, gets NA rather population-prediction. Different values recorded time treated replicate measurements. fit gets status: "ok"; "warning" lme4::lmer() warned (e.g. convergence) fit singular (lme4::isSingular()); "failed" subjects lme4::lmer() gave error. Failed fits give NA variable landmark without affecting fits, warning lists every fit "ok". automatic fallback random slope random intercept. Standard errors second-stage survival model treat LME-derived values known, understate uncertainty.

title: Two-stage bootstrap for propagating uncertainty from LME predictions — bootstrap_landmark
text: bootstrap_landmark() bootstraps complete landmark workflow. replicate, risk set every landmark resampled replacement, user's pipeline re-run resampled data (refitting longitudinal mixed-effects models, regenerating predictions landmark refitting landmark survival models), coefficients collected. bootstrap distribution quantifies uncertainty estimating longitudinal trajectories propagation landmark survival models, standard errors fit_landmark() ignore. Results reported percentile confidence intervals, percentile bootstrap p-values median bootstrap distribution, next full-data fit.

title: Two-stage bootstrap for propagating uncertainty from LME predictions — bootstrap_landmark
code: bootstrap_landmark(   baseline,   pipeline,   n_boot = 200,   exponentiate = FALSE,   conf.level = 0.95,   alternative = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),   progress = getOption("tidylandmark.progress", interactive()) )

title: Two-stage bootstrap for propagating uncertainty from LME predictions — bootstrap_landmark
text: baseline landmark_tbl, returned landmark_data(). pipeline function one argument, landmark_tbl, runs rest workflow (e.g. add_landmark_covariates() fit_landmark()) returns landmark_fit. n_boot Number bootstrap replicates. Default 200. exponentiate TRUE, report hazard ratios (subdistribution hazard ratios Fine-Gray models) instead log hazard ratios. conf.level Confidence level intervals. Default 0.95. alternative Alternative hypothesis bootstrap p-values: one "two.sided" (default), "greater" "less". progress Show progress bar replicates? what: tidylandmark: Tidy Workflows for Landmark Survival Analysis — tidylandmark-package
title: tidylandmark: Tidy Workflows for Landmark Survival Analysis — tidylandmark-package
text: Provides tidy framework landmark survival analysis, facilitating construction landmark-specific risk sets, incorporation longitudinal covariates, estimation associations time--event outcomes. Supports covariate estimation using last observation carried forward (LOCF) linear mixed-effects models (LME), alongside Cox proportional hazards Fine-Gray competing risks regression. Offers consistent reproducible workflow conducting analyses across multiple landmark times.

title: tidylandmark 0.0.0.9000 (development version)
text: Implemented landmark_data(), constructs landmark risk sets optional user-supplied time horizon. Implemented add_landmark_covariates(), attaches pre-landmark values longitudinal variables subject-landmark row. Variables selected locf use last non-missing value (optionally within lookback window); variables selected lme use subject-specific predictions linear mixed-effects model fitted separately variable landmark, options lme_args (random slope, adjustment terms, lmerControl()). Implemented fit_landmark(), fits independent Cox, cause-specific, Fine-Gray model landmark. Implemented bootstrap_landmark(), resamples landmark’s risk set, re-runs user-supplied pipeline (mixed models, predictions survival models) every replicate, reports percentile intervals p-values account uncertainty LME-derived covariates.
